newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore urges politician to aid death threat probe.
newsitem.headline: Singapore urges politician to aid death threat probe.

text.p: Singapore police on Wednesday urged an opposition politician who fled to Malaysia after receiving death threats to help with their investigation.

A police statement said Tang Liang Hong, accused by Prime Minister Goh Chock Tong during the campaign for last week's general elections of being a "Chinese chauvinist", had not handed over one of two threatening letters.

Tang's daughter, Kelly, had given police a letter saying merely "Death Sentence God's Will". But Tang, a defeated Workers' Party candidate, had not handed over a four-paragraph letter he had faxed to top Singapore newspapers, the statement said.

"Mr Tang should contact CID (the Criminal Investigation Department) as soon as possible to assist in investigating the threats," the statement said. "Investigation on the threats cannot be carried out through newspapers."
Tang fled to Malaysia after the elections in which he was Goh's main target.
Goh said Tang and his views were dangerous to multi-racial Singapore, where 77 percent of the population is ethnic Chinese. There are significant Malay and Tamil minorities.
Tang was part of a five-member Workers' Party ticket in a winner-take-all, multi-member constituency where his party was thought to have its best chance of winning.
Goh's People's Action Party (PAP) won the constituency and its five seats in the 83-member parliament with 54 percent of the vote, well below its national average of 65 percent.
The PAP won all but two seats in the poll.
